tests.name: Effective description
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed)

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense and domain-specific throughout — it does not explain general concepts like what CloudWatch or FSx are, but jumps straight into non-obvious rules (e.g. how to resolve the file system id, how to label severity, the write-boundary rules). It is verbose in places but every sentence carries specific, non-generic instruction.
tests.evidence: "Never ask for a fact the AWS API can enumerate." is a domain-specific instruction, not a general concept explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (thresholds, metric catalogs, CLI command packs, error tables) is consistently delegated to references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even inside conditional/decision-tree sections like the routing table.
tests.evidence: "Thresholds and severity bands live there — don't paraphrase them from memory." shows detail is deliberately kept out of the body.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ (REFERENCE.md, cloudtrail-audit.md, cloudwatch-metrics.md, dependencies-and-errors.md, deployment-types.md, ontap-cli-pack.md, review-checks.md, unlisted-symptoms.md) has a markdown link in the body, confirmed again in the final References section.
tests.evidence: "[dependencies-and-errors.md](references/dependencies-and-errors.md) — service dependency map and error handling."

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Links to reference files are consistently paired with explicit trigger conditions (e.g. a routing table keyed by symptom, or 'before quoting any ceiling... read deployment-types.md').
tests.evidence: "Deployment type before any number." ... "then read [deployment-types.md](references/deployment-types.md)" specifies exactly when to load it.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (write boundary, severity labeling, metric collection order) are prescriptive and exact, while flexible analytical judgment (interpreting findings, routing to the right reference) is given reasoned explanation rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "Never attempt a write. Never offer to." is prescriptive for a fragile boundary, while "Separate observed from inferred" gives reasoning-based guidance for judgment calls.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple tool calls are discussed (e.g. capacity metrics), the skill prescribes an exact sequence/default rather than presenting equal alternatives; no genuine multi-tool menu is left ambiguous.
tests.evidence: "Read usable SSD, never derive it: usable = StorageCapacity, free = StorageCapacity − StorageUsed." establishes one definitive approach, not competing options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic approach (identify target, collect config/metrics, run checks, assign severity, report) that applies to any FSx ONTAP file system, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Track progress through these steps. Every run completes Steps 1–3 and 6" describes a reusable procedure, not a single declared task.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill is saturated with concrete, non-obvious corrections throughout (false-signal suppression, Region pitfalls, fs- id ambiguity with EFS, utilization >100% meaning bursting) that function as gotchas even without a dedicated heading.
tests.evidence: "Utilization above 100% means bursting above baseline, not a data error, and Data*OperationTime is in seconds."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defines a structured report template (Summary, Findings, Change history, Recommendations, Data gaps, Escalation packet, Appendix) for its output.
tests.evidence: "Produce a Markdown report named fsx-ontap-review-<fsid>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md" followed by the full section outline.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The report template outline in Step 5 is short (bullet list of section names, well under 20 lines) with no large inline skeleton; detailed formatting rules live in review-checks.md.
tests.evidence: "- Summary — ... - Findings — table: finding, evidence, severity, impact. - Change history — ... - Recommendations — ... - Data gaps — ... - Escalation-readiness packet — ... - Appendix — ..."

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The only asset file, sample-fsx-context.json, is explicitly linked in the body.
tests.evidence: "use [sample-fsx-context.json](assets/sample-fsx-context.json) as the working context so the review can still be demonstrated end to end."

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The link to the asset specifies exactly when to use it — only when no live access is available.
tests.evidence: "If no live access is available, use [sample-fsx-context.json](assets/sample-fsx-context.json) as the working context"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and the detailed sections below each use matching '## Step N:' headings.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms" ... followed by "## Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms" as a matching detailed section.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 6 is an explicit self-validation checklist instructing the agent to check its own draft report against multiple correctness criteria before sending.
tests.evidence: "Check your own draft against this list and fix anything that fails before sending:" followed by items like "Every figure the user quoted... was verified against the API or metrics and reported as confirmed or corrected".
